title: Web Push notifications
description: Send Web Push notifications from your server with Web Crypto only: RFC 8291 aes128gcm payload encryption, VAPID (RFC 8292) signing and key generation, per-user subscriptions with endpoint allow-list and dedupe, TTL/urgency/topic headers, cleanup of expired subscriptions on 404/410, bounded-concurrency fan-out, a PostgreSQL store, a Fetch adapter and a same-origin service worker snippet.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Web Crypto (ECDH, ECDSA, HKDF and AES-GCM on P-256), TextEncoder, btoa/atob and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route. The service worker snippet is plain JavaScript for the browser.
No runtime packages (no web-push npm dependency), environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Run generateVapidKeys() once, store the private key as a server secret and pass {publicKey, privateKey, subject} (a mailto: or https: contact) to createWebPush; rotating the keys invalidates every existing subscription.
On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlPushSubscriptionStore with your query executor; on other databases implement PushSubscriptionStore keyed by endpoint with an atomic failure counter.
Pass the platform fetch; keep the default push service host allow-list unless you serve browsers with other push services, then set allowedHosts or allowAnyHttpsEndpoint.
Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token and mount createWebPushHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy.

Put serviceWorkerSnippet in your service worker file and subscribe in the page with pushManager.subscribe({userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey}) using the key from GET {prefix}/vapid-public-key.
Call send or sendMany from server jobs; retry rate-limited and server-error results after retryAfterSeconds with your queue.
limitations: Writes one aes128gcm record, so payloads are limited to 3,993 bytes; send a short message and let the page fetch details. The legacy aesgcm encoding and GCM API keys are not supported.

Does not queue or retry; rate-limited (429), server-error (5xx) and network-error results are returned for your job runner to retry. Subscriptions are deleted only on 404/410; failure_count is recorded but never acted on.
Tested against RFC 8291/8292 vectors and fake push services, not against live FCM, Mozilla, Apple or Windows push services; those services and browser permission prompts need an in-app check.
The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs one connection, not on every hosted Postgres under parallel load.
No rate limiting on the subscription routes and no per-notification preferences; combine with the rate-limit and notification-preferences modules.
Production key custody, database correctness, session security and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: routes: GET {prefix}/vapid-public-key, POST|DELETE {prefix}/subscriptions; sending is server code only
payload max 3,993 bytes; default urgency normal; VAPID JWT expires after 12 h
endpoints limited to known push hosts (422 endpoint-not-allowed); 20 subscriptions per user
a 404 or 410 from the push service deletes the subscription

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/web-push.test.mjs tests/web-push-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: encryption reproduces the RFC 8291 Section 5 / Appendix A example header, ciphertext and body bytes exactly
an independent receiver-side decryptor recovers the plaintext; each message uses a fresh salt and ephemeral key
a 3,993-byte payload fills exactly 4,096 octets; larger payloads, wrong auth length and off-curve keys are refused
VAPID keys generate as 65/32 octets; the ES256 JWT has aud = push service origin, sub and exp, and its raw 64-byte r||s signature verifies with Web Crypto
VAPID lifetime is capped at 24 hours, the subject must be mailto: or https:, and a mismatched key pair is refused
subscriptions require https endpoints on allow-listed push hosts (or any https when configured), a valid P-256 p256dh and a 16-octet auth, and dedupe on endpoint
send posts TTL, Urgency, Topic, Content-Encoding aes128gcm and vapid t=, k= authorization, and the browser can decrypt the body
ttl, urgency, topic (1 to 32 base64url characters) and payload size are validated before any request is sent
201/202 are sent, 404/410 delete the subscription, 413 is too-large, 429 reports retry-after seconds or date, 400/401/403 are vapid-error, 5xx and network failures increment failure_count
sendMany dedupes users and never exceeds the configured concurrency
HTTP adapter: public key route, subscribe, owner-only unsubscribe, origin check, 401 when signed out, bounded bodies and cache-control no-store
service worker snippet shows notifications and opens or focuses same-origin URLs only, refusing cross-origin, javascript:, data: and scheme-changing URLs
schema.sql applies; upsert keeps created_at and resets failures; concurrent subscribes of one endpoint leave one row
a 410 from the push service deletes the row; six concurrent removals have one winner and 20 concurrent failures count exactly 20

changes: First release: RFC 8291 encryption, VAPID, subscriptions and delivery, in-memory and PostgreSQL stores, Fetch adapter and service worker snippet.
